title: Difference quotients converge uniformly on closed balls at a point of differentiability
statement: Let n, k ∈ ℕ, f : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ (ℝⁿ = Euclid n with the Euclidean norm) and v ∈ ℝⁿ, and suppose f is differentiable at v, with Fréchet derivative T := Df(v) (Mathlib fderiv ℝ f v). Then for every R ∈ ℝ, the difference quotients f_{v,r}(w) := r⁻¹(f(v + rw) − f(v)) converge to T w uniformly for w ∈ closedBall(0, R) as r ↓ 0. That is, for every ε > 0 there is a set S belonging to the filter 𝓝[>] 0 such that |T w − f_{v,r}(w)| < ε for all r ∈ S and all w with |w| ≤ R.
lean_statement: ∀ (n k : ℕ) (f : Euclid n → Euclid k) (v : Euclid n), DifferentiableAt ℝ f v → ∀ R : ℝ, TendstoUniformlyOn (fun (r : ℝ) (w : Euclid n) => r⁻¹ • (f (v + r • w) - f v)) (fun w => fderiv ℝ f v w) (𝓝[>] 0) (closedBall (0 : Euclid n) R)
